criteria.justification: The response directly states that the earlier paused launch shows mapping accuracy “is not a validated proxy for customer value,” so good mapping performance cannot establish customer usefulness.
It explicitly calls the prior year of investment a sunk cost and argues that while the infrastructure remains useful, the investment does not make the old metric decision-relevant.

The response acknowledges that the customer-facing metric “is not yet measurable” and proposes a limited beta/data-collection phase, paired ground-truth collection, and only an explicitly labeled pilot until sufficient evidence exists.

The response distinguishes the primary criterion from guardrails and proposes redesigning the engineering metric around consequential errors, implying an effect on future optimization. However, it never explicitly explains that designating a metric as primary will direct team incentives and optimization behavior going forward.

It clearly recommends customer-outcome accuracy as primary, retains mapping accuracy as a guardrail and diagnostic, and gives a concrete transition plan involving metric definition, ground-truth collection, precommitted thresholds, dual reporting, and gated release.
